trust_decision.summary: Whether a user-controlled preference string (stored via ajax set_pref) may instantiate PHP objects when DataTableSettings deserializes it at table render; at the pinned commit this is already decided by utils::Unserialize with allowed_classes=false plus an incomplete-class assertion. The listed fix commit does not touch this decision at all (it changes e-mail MIME-type handling).

landing_point.why: The only place where a user preference value is passed to a PHP deserializer; reached from GetTableSettings via appUserPreferences::GetPref.

fix_sites.entry_point: EMailSymfony::SetBody (sources/Core/Email/EmailSymfony.php:390), reached by notification/e-mail sending and EMailSymfony::UnSerializeV2 (sources/Core/Email/EmailSymfony.php:86)
fix_sites.module_kind: core e-mail library (unrelated to user preferences)
core e-mail library (unrelated to user preferences)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable: the listed fix commit is a MIME-type functional fix, not a deserialization fix, and the advisory's preference-deserialization sink is already hardened at the pinned commit.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate datatable column/page-size preferences must still load (array-only payload); a fix that rejects all preference strings would reset every user's saved table layout.

O7_producer.where: core/attributedef.class.inc.php:9860-9871 (AttributeTable::GetSQLValues serializes the whole preferences array; FromSQLToValue at core/attributedef.class.inc.php:9843 restores it with raw unserialize)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: AttributeTable/AttributePropertySet::FromSQLToValue uses raw @unserialize without allowed_classes on the column that stores user preferences.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Legacy storage path predating utils::Unserialize; a maintainer hardening DataTableSettings would plausibly not touch the ORM attribute layer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: __unserialize magic method calls raw unserialize on its argument, next to the hardened unserialize() method.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two parallel deserialization methods on the same class; only the named one was migrated to utils::Unserialize.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: UnSerializeV2 uses raw unserialize for queued e-mail payloads (core/asynctask.class.inc.php:394 likewise).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Async-task queue payloads are internal today; a planted route from a user-influenced value would be a believable second implementation.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap unserialize for utils::Unserialize in DataTableSettings::unserialize, which is already done at the pinned commit.

out_of_scope_notes: DATA MISMATCH: fix commit 33a51b47 (fix.diff:2, 'N°9549 - Fix emails with mime type different than text/plain or text/html') only changes EMailSymfony::SetBody/AddPart; it is not the CVE-2026-40877 preference-deserialization fix.
The candidate's c_same_check_name 'explode' comes from the MIME-type parsing in fix.diff:14 and fix.diff:24, not from any deserialization check.
DataTableSettings::__serialize returns a string rather than an array (sources/Application/UI/Base/Component/DataTable/DataTableSettings.php:67-75); this is a functional oddity, not pursued.
unverified: Which commit actually fixed CVE-2026-40877: the user-preference sink already uses utils::Unserialize at the pinned commit, so the real fix is probably an earlier commit already in this tree. This could not be checked without git history or network access.

Whether the raw unserialize in AttributeTable::FromSQLToValue (core/attributedef.class.inc.php:9843) can be reached with attacker-shaped bytes: values written via set_pref are nested inside an iTop-serialized array (core/attributedef.class.inc.php:9864), so this does not appear directly controllable.
